ending_first.ending: In the hall outside Room 303 of the Heart O' The City Hotel, Agent Smith shoots Neo three times point-blank in the chest and Agent Brown confirms him dead while, in the real world aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, his monitors flatline and Sentinels breach the hull as Morpheus reaches for the EMP. Trinity refuses to accept it, takes hold of his body and kisses him, and his heart restarts. Neo opens his eyes in the hall, now able to see the Matrix as flowing green code, raises a hand and halts the Agents' volley of bullets in mid-air, then lets Smith shoot him again before entering Smith's body from inside and bursting him apart — the first Agent ever destroyed, so the surviving Agents feel fear. With Sentinels descending on Morpheus at the EMP switch, Neo sprints for a ringing phone in the hall and dives through the line at Trinity's call of 'Now!' an instant before the EMP would have to fire, waking on the ship in Trinity's arms. Later, alone in a city phone booth, he speaks as someone no longer running, hangs up, and rises into flight above the skyscrapers.

s01.text: Thomas A. Anderson — called Neo when he hacks at night — lives doubled. By day he endures the downtown offices of Meta CorTechs, where his boss Rhineheart lectures him about lateness and authority and he answers with flat, exhausted compliance; by night he sits sleepless at his PC haunted by the question 'What is the Matrix?' When his own screen types to him and tells him to follow the white rabbit, he is wary but curious. At a disk deal for two grand, he notices a small white rabbit pin on Dujour's black leather jacket and, against his plan to work the next day, goes with Choi and Dujour to a crowded gathering. There Trinity — a leather-clad ghost in close-fitting black whose speed makes armed cops fail to register her until too late — finds him by name, knows his hacker handle, and warns him that someone is watching. She is calm and unreadable, and her warning turns his private dread into a hunt that now knows his name.

s02.text: The hunt closes the next morning. A softpak delivers a ringing phone and Morpheus's voice, a tall, still man whose certainty can light a room, guides Neo turn by turn through the office — into an empty cubicle, down a row, into an office on the left — toward a window ledge he cannot force himself to cross, and Agents take him. In an interrogation room Agent Smith, pale and immaculately composed with ice-blue eyes behind sunglasses, lays out Neo's two lives and offers to wipe his record clean for Morpheus; when Neo refuses with contempt, Smith shows what the system can do: Neo's mouth seals smooth and a fiber-optic wire-tap animates into an insect-like fluke-worm that burrows into his navel. He wakes as if from a nightmare to a ringing phone and a voice calling him 'the One' demanding a single 'Yes.' On the rain-slick Adams Street bridge a car slides to a stop — Switch holding a large gun and Apoc driving, with Trinity insisting the gun is for their protection from him. In the moving car Trinity seals a steel-and-glass extractor over his navel and, when suction fails, drives current through him until the bug rockets into a glass cage and reverts to a plain wire-tap on the pavement. At room 1313 of the Hotel Lafayette, Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong dread as a real enslaving system and offers two pills: blue to forget, red to know. Neo swallows the red. The cracked oval mirror liquefies and crawls into him, his heart arrests, and the coaxial cable locked into the base of his skull tears free as a machine severs him from magenta amnion in a tower of glowing pods and flushes him through waste pipes and sewer mains until a metallic cable snatches him into the hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar, where Morpheus has his atrophied body rebuilt.

s03.text: Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, Morpheus walks Neo — jacked in (plugged via the socket at the skull) into the Construct, a loading program that renders the simulation — through the desert of the real: the world he knew is a neural-interactive simulation of America at the end of the twentieth century, the sky was scorched to deny machines solar power, and humans are grown as batteries in fields of amnion-filled pods stacked in towers, while the last free humans survive in Zion, a city deep underground near the earth's core. The ship itself must hide in sewer mains from Sentinels, squid-like hunting machines that track its electromagnetic wake, with only one weapon — an EMP (electromagnetic pulse) that kills electrics but cannot be fired while anyone is still jacked in. Morpheus tells Neo a prophecy from the Oracle that the One will free humanity and declares the search is over, and Tank — the ship's operator, a solid, muscular Black man with an easy grin who runs the consoles — begins loading combat programs directly into Neo's brain. Neo absorbs kung fu and jujitsu in hours and believes he can fight, but in the white-floored dojo Morpheus dismantles every furious, technique-driven assault and beats him to the floor to prove a rule: some laws can be bent, others broken, only if the mind is freed. On a rooftop jump program Morpheus crosses an impossible gap to demonstrate; Neo runs and falls badly short, the yielding ground catching him and leaving blood in his hand, while the crew watches split between doubters and believers and Trinity's quiet hope breaks her reserve before she leaves. On a crowded downtown street that is itself a training program, Morpheus freezes time around an Agent to teach that Agents — sentient programs including Smith, Brown and Jones, tall, broad-shouldered men with shaved heads and flat, unreadable faces — can move in and out of any person still hardwired to the system, and that anyone not freed is a potential Agent.

s04.text: Not everyone can carry that truth. Cypher — close-cropped dark hair, trimmed goatee, tinted glasses, called Mr. Reagan inside the program — pours Dozer's clear alcohol on the main deck and recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count, telling Neo five before him died taking on an Agent because Morpheus got them believing, then slips into the Matrix to a restaurant where he savors an impossible steak and wine and bargains with Smith to be reinserted rich and ignorant. When Morpheus takes the crew through the Hotel Lafayette to reach the Oracle, Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in an alley garbage can. In a vast tenement building the Oracle lives behind an apartment door; on the way up Morpheus confesses he misunderstood her about the five failures. Inside, a priestess lets Neo wait with a skinny Spoon Boy who bends a spoon by seeing there is no spoon, then the Oracle — an old woman — tells Neo privately he is not the One and that he will have to choose between his life and Morpheus's, ordering him to keep it to himself. As they leave, a black cat repeats — deja vu — which Tank recognizes as the Matrix being rewritten, a trace program fixing their signal after Trinity's earlier call was captured at #312-555. The trap springs: Mouse is cornered and killed in Room 1313 while cops sweep floor by floor, and Tank guides the rest by voice into Room 808 where they smash a man-sized hole into the main wet-wall and worm down stack pipes. In the wall an Agent ambushes Neo; Morpheus bursts through, pins the Agent, and orders Trinity to get Neo out, giving himself up so they can escape. In the basement mechanical room under grenade fire, Trinity finds a catch-basin grate and pries it open, but Morpheus is overwhelmed — head-butting Smith before being taken — and is carried to a government building for interrogation.

s05.text: The Agents — Smith, Brown and Jones — hold Morpheus in an executive office on the government building's roof, flanked by Marines, and double the serum dosage until his alpha pattern flattens into an ordered wave, the sign he is about to break and give up Zion's codes, while he spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking. Meanwhile the survivors surface onto a back street through the wall and re-establish contact by radio: Trinity climbs out with Neo, Tank takes calls on the ship, and they learn Morpheus is alive but being moved. Cypher has already reached the exit — a ringing phone in the back room of an abandoned TV repair shop at Franklin and Erie, reached through a window — and on the ship his body jerks awake in its harness, draws a concealed rifle, shoots Tank and leaves him for dead, then answers Trinity's call with a false story of an accident. Once Apoc, Switch, Neo and Trinity are jacked back in, Cypher murders Apoc and Switch where they hang comatose, delivers Morpheus's location to the Agents, and stands over Neo's and Trinity's still bodies to force an answer from Trinity before Tank — alive despite his wounds — returns armed and strikes him down. Neo and Trinity wake in the shop; Neo breaks free of Trinity's embrace and sends her out first when the phone rings, and back on the main deck Trinity is unplugged, sits upright, names Dozer and, reading Tank's face, understands Dozer too is dead, her relief turning to grief.

s06.text: On the deck Neo stops Tank from pulling Morpheus's plug and says he is going back in to bring Morpheus out alive. He denies he is the One, so the mission is not a prophecy but a wager on a man — something he cannot justify logically, only believe — and Trinity, gutted by Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial, converts grief into command and insists on going with him, while Tank opens racks of weapons and an earphone. The assault is one continuous action from the lobby through the elevator to the roof: they gun through guards in the lobby, ride the elevator, duel Agent Jones on the rooftop, and call Tank for a pilot program so Trinity can load the ability to fly a helicopter. Neo drops the helicopter onto the executive office, guns down Jones, Brown and Smith, and finds Morpheus unresponsive until he forces him awake; Morpheus bolts for the window and Smith shoots him in the leg mid-dive, but Neo leaps after him and catches his handcuffed wrist before he hits the ground while Trinity swings the helicopter under them on a climbing rope and rain gutter. On the roof afterward Tank's watch resolves into certainty about the One; Neo tries to report what the Oracle told him, but Morpheus cuts him off and reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation, then Tank secures a hardwired ringing phone as their exit and Morpheus and Neo set out toward it while Brown reports the trace has fixed their position and Jones orders a Sentinel strike on the ship.

s07.text: Smith withdraws from the other Agents in disgust, insisting the quarry is not gone, and senses them below. In a graffiti-covered subway station Morpheus answers a ringing phone and exits first through the line, Trinity follows a breath before Smith — who has revealed himself from an old drunk in the corner — can shoot her, leaving a shattered booth. Tank refuses Trinity's demand to be sent back; Neo is left alone before a dead escalator. On the ship Morpheus, Trinity and Tank watch scrolling code while Neo, urged to run, turns back from the escalator to face Smith with a gunfighter's calm that Morpheus reads as the beginning of belief. Their gunfight clicks empty, then they trade bare-handed blows until Smith chokes Neo by the electrified third rail and uses the arriving train to frame his death as inevitability, pronouncing a name and fate Neo refuses; Neo summons an impossible surge, hurls Smith into the tunnel ceiling, and breaks free as the train barrels over him, only for Smith to rise again. Neo snatches a businessman's cell phone mid-sprint through the city and, guided by Tank's voice, runs a gauntlet where every block tightens — open market filling with Agents at every turn, a dead-end alley forcing him to kick through an apartment building and break a locked door — toward the Heart O' The City Hotel. Across from its faded neon sign Smith suddenly registers the place and locks on, while aboard the Nebuchadnezzar Tank loads the exit and Morpheus drives the escape until the lights go red and Sentinels slam the hull. In the alley Neo climbs a fire escape under fire as Brown and Jones close behind; he breaks through a third-floor window into a hall and races toward door 303 as Trinity drives him to hurry, and is stopped cold by Smith's point-blank shot.

s08.text: Three chest shots in hall 303 drop Neo and Brown confirms him gone; on the ship the life monitors flatline and the crew gives him up even as Sentinels overrun the main deck and descend on Morpheus at the EMP switch, which he cannot throw while Neo is still jacked in. Trinity refuses the ending the system has written: she takes hold of Neo's body, speaks to him, and kisses him, and the monitors jump back to life. Neo's eyes snap open in the hall, revived, and he now reads the room as flowing code; he raises a hand and halts the Agents' volley in mid-air. Aboard the ship the crew watches him blaze across the screens and Morpheus declares him the One as an explosion rocks the hull. In the hall Neo lets Smith come close, enters him and bursts out from inside, destroying the first Agent ever so the surviving Agents feel fear for the first time. Sentinels overrun the deck, jolting Trinity from awe into a single urgent summons to get up; on a screen Neo appears as a rushing stream of code diving for the ringing phone in the hall, and at Trinity's 'Now!' — timed to that dive — he charges toward its source and exits through the line an instant before Morpheus would have to fire the EMP. In the darkened hovercraft Trinity's vigil breaks as Neo wakes at her voice, reaches for her, and she weeps as she kisses him, releasing the grief she held while watching over his body, before he later stands alone in a hall, steps into a city phone booth, and rises into open flight above the skyscrapers, no longer running.

jacket_copy: Thomas A. Anderson lives two lives. By day he is a compliant coder at Meta CorTechs. By night he is Neo, a sleepless hacker haunted by a single question: What is the Matrix? A message on his own PC, a white rabbit pin, and a leather-clad ghost named Trinity pull him through the looking glass — into a world where Agents in immaculate suits can possess anyone still plugged in, where a ringing phone is the only way out, and where the sky above is a lie. Morpheus, the insurgent captain who has staked everything on a prophecy about the One, offers Neo a choice that cannot be unfollowed. To take it is to see humans farmed in towers of amnion, a last city called Zion holding beneath a scorched earth, and a hovercraft called the Nebuchadnezzar hunted through sewer mains by Sentinels that hear every pulse. Training will break him. The Oracle will tell him what he doesn't want to hear. And a crewmate who prefers a perfect steak to a hard truth will trade them all to be plugged back in. To free the man who freed him, Neo must re-enter the system that kills anyone who fights it — and learn whether belief can bend the rules that bind him.
